current_formulation: Researchers keep both equivalence and emphasis frames and state which type they study; the records reach this step through a 2025 secondary source.

steps.formulation: A frame is an interpretive design that a person uses to make sense of events (Goffman 1974, through a secondary account).
steps.quote: Goffman called these interpretive designs frames that we use in our day-to-day experience to make sense of the world.

criticism.quote: framing is often defined casually, with much left to an assumed tacit understanding of reader and researcher.

steps.formulation: To frame is to select some aspects of reality and make them more salient in a text, promoting a problem definition, causal interpretation, moral evaluation, or treatment recommendation.
steps.quote: To frame is to select some aspects of a perceived reality and make them more salient in a communicating text

criticism.quote: it has been argued that effects of emphasis frames may not be exclusively attributed to framing

steps.formulation: Researchers should move away from studying emphasis frames, which overlap with agenda setting and priming. A4-SR-08 reports these calls and cites Cacciatore, Scheufele and Iyengar (2016) and Scheufele and Iyengar (2012) for them.
steps.quote: there have been calls to move away from studying emphasis frames

criticism.quote: frames that seem equivalent may actually not always be equivalent

steps.formulation: Both frame types stay in use (Brüggemann and D'Angelo 2018; Leeper and Slothuus 2018, through a secondary account).
steps.quote: Still, there are also good reasons to keep studying both
